author: GamingBolt
description:
Ultimately, Toy Story: Retro Roundup succeeds as a preservation effort. It's great to have these games playable on modern consoles in one convenient package. 

There's plenty of content here, and some of it remains genuinely enjoyable, but a little more care could have turned a fun nostalgia trip into something even more special.
title: Toy Story: Retro Roundup Review - An Excellent Preservation Effort

author: GamingBolt
description:
Enshrouded leaves Early Access with more varied combat and a broader range of zones and dungeons that make exploring Embervale more rewarding. And if you’re worried that all of these changes mean that the survival crafting aspects have been left behind, you have nothing to worry about. 

Enshrouded has only further refined what was already a phenomenal freeform building system by making it more accessible with, for example, giving the player the ability to fly while building, and tuning the material costs. In what some might call its “finished” state, Enshrouded feels like one of the best survival crafting games in the market right now.
title: Enshrouded 1.0 Review - One of the Best Survival Action Role-Playing Games

author: GamingBolt
description:
There isn't a rumor mill out there that Grand Theft Auto 6, much less Rockstar Games, hasn't been a part of. But with the open-world epic about a month away, and so many details revealed, it felt like nothing could really grab our attention at this point. That is, except for one rumor, one so precious that we didn't even consider its possibility: A release window (allegedly) for the PC version.

According to GamesBeat, GTA 6 will launch for the platform in Q1 2027. And in case there's any confusion, it explicitly claimed “within the first three months” of next year, according to four different “industry sources.” That's it – nothing more, and naturally, Rockstar Games didn't respond for comment.
title: GTA 6’s Reported PC Release Could Break Rockstar’s Long-Wait Tradition

author: GamingBolt
description:
Mafia 3: Definitive Edition for PS5 might seem like not much has changed since its latest update, but spend some time with it, and you’re going to see it looks and feels so much better thanks to better framerates and improved visuals that come with a lot of polish. 
The result is an experience that takes a strong story and enjoyable combat, despite a repetitive mission structure, and presents them so well it’s easy to forget you’re playing a ten-year-old game.

Of course, reminders of its age do crop up from time to time, as do the same issues of poor pacing and repetition that are fundamental flaws in its design. However, it’s been a blast playing Mafia 3 again with all these improvements despite those flaws. We’ve dived deep into why, so jump right in as we take you for a drive on what's new in New Bordeaux.
title: Mafia 3 PS5 Review - Is It Finally Worth It?
